questions.question: A centre code database uses a log-structured merge tree (LSM tree) with 4 levels. If level 0 can hold 100 entries and each subsequent level is 10 times larger, what is the total capacity?
questions.solution:
A **Log-Structured Merge Tree (LSM tree)** is a data structure used by many modern databases to provide high-performance writes. It organizes data into multiple **levels**, where each level has a specific capacity.

 
• The problem specifies that there are **4 levels** in total, starting from **Level 0**.
 
• The capacity of **Level 0** is **100 entries**.
 
• Each subsequent level is **10 times larger** than the previous one.

We can calculate the capacity of each level as follows:

 
• **Level 0:** 100 entries
 
• **Level 1:** 100 × 10 = 1,000 entries
 
• **Level 2:** 1,000 × 10 = 10,000 entries
 
• **Level 3:** 10,000 × 10 = 100,000 entries

**
Total Capacity = 100 + 1,000 + 10,000 + 100,000 = **1,11,100**.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 2**”.

questions.question: A man is 24 years older than his son. In two years, his age will be twice the age of his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference between Man and Son = **24 years**.

Condition: In 2 years, Man's age = 2 × Son's age.

**Formula Used:**

Age after 'n' years = Present Age + n

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **present age** of the son be **x** years.

⇒ Then, the **present age** of the man = **(x + 24)** years.

⇒ Age of the son after 2 years = **(x + 2)** years.

⇒ Age of the man after 2 years = (x + 24) + 2 = **(x + 26)** years.

⇒ According to the question: (x + 26) = 2 × (x + 2)

⇒ x + 26 = 2x + 4

⇒ 2x − x = 26 − 4

⇒ x = **22****

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 2**”.

options.text: Economic instability and lack of social support.

questions.solution:

• The rankings are based on a three-year average of life evaluations. For the 2025 report, data from **2022 to 2024** was analyzed.

• **Finland** continues to hold the title of the **happiest country in the world** for the eighth consecutive year in 2025, followed by other Nordic nations like **Denmark** and **Iceland**.

• The report evaluates countries based on six key variables: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **freedom from corruption**.

• The **International Day of Happiness** is celebrated annually on **March 20th**, the day the report is typically released.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT refer to reserve money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Savings money**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Reserve Money**, also known as **M0**, is the most fundamental measure of the money supply in **India**, representing the total monetary liabilities of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.

• It is widely referred to as **Central Bank Money** because it consists of currency and deposits that are directly issued or held by the **Central Bank**. *Hence, statement 1 refers to reserve money.*

• The term **Base Money** is used because it forms the foundation upon which the entire money supply of the **economy** is built through the **banking system**. *Hence, statement 2 refers to reserve money.*

• It is also known as **High-Powered Money** because it has a multiplier effect on the total money supply; a small increase in **Reserve Money** can lead to a much larger increase in the total money supply through **bank lending**. *Hence, statement 3 refers to reserve money.*

• **Savings money**, typically referring to deposits in **savings accounts**, is a component of **Narrow Money (M1)** or **Broad Money (M3)**. It represents a liability of **commercial banks** to the public, not a liability of the **RBI**. *Hence, statement 4 does NOT refer to reserve money and is the correct answer.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Components of Reserve Money (M0)**: It includes **Currency in Circulation**, **Bankers' Deposits with RBI**, and **'Other' Deposits with RBI**. It is the most liquid measure of money from the perspective of the **Central Bank**.

• **Narrow Money (M1)**: This includes **Currency with the Public**, **Demand Deposits** with the banking system (such as **savings** and **current accounts**), and **'Other' Deposits with RBI**. It is highly liquid and used for immediate transactions.

• **Intermediate Money (M2)**: This is calculated as **M1** plus **Savings Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks**. This measure was more prominent before the **1998** working group recommendations.

• **Broad Money (M3)**: This is the most commonly used measure of money supply in **India**. It is calculated as **M1** plus **Time Deposits** (such as **Fixed Deposits**) with the banking system. It reflects the total volume of money available in the **economy**.

• **M4 Classification**: This includes **M3** plus **Total Deposits with Post Office Savings Organizations** (excluding **National Savings Certificates**).

**Important Points__**

• **Money Multiplier**: This is the ratio of **Broad Money (M3)** to **Reserve Money (M0)**. It indicates the capacity of the **banking system** to create money. If the **RBI** increases the **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**, the **money multiplier** usually decreases.

• **Monetary Policy Tools**: The **RBI** manages **Reserve Money** through various instruments like **Open Market Operations (OMO)**, **Repo Rate**, and **Reverse Repo Rate** to control **inflation** and **liquidity**.

• **Historical Context**: The current classification of money aggregates (**M0, M1, M2, M3**) was introduced based on the recommendations of the **Second Working Group on Money Supply** in **1977**.

• **Sources of Reserve Money**: The primary sources include **Net RBI Credit to the Government**, **RBI Credit to the Commercial Sector**, **RBI's Net Foreign Exchange Assets**, and **Government's Currency Liabilities to the Public**.

• **Liquidity Aggregates**: In addition to **M0-M3**, the **RBI** also tracks **L1, L2, and L3**, which include broader financial instruments like **term deposits** with financial institutions and **public deposits** with **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**.
</ul

questions.question: Which government scheme aims to provide a social safety net by guaranteeing wage employment to rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** was enacted in **September 2005** and is one of the largest work guarantee programs in the world. It provides a **legal guarantee** for at least **100 days** of wage employment in every **financial year** to every **rural household** whose adult members volunteer to do **unskilled manual work**.

• The core objective of the scheme is to enhance **livelihood security** in rural areas by providing a safety net for the poor, while simultaneously creating **durable assets** such as roads, ponds, and irrigation canals to improve rural infrastructure.

• The act establishes a **demand-driven** model where the government is legally obligated to provide work within **15 days** of a demand being made. If the government fails to provide employment within this period, the applicant is entitled to a daily **unemployment allowance**.

• To promote **social inclusion** and **gender equality**, the act mandates that at least **one-third** of the total beneficiaries must be **women** who have registered and requested work under the scheme.

• Employment is provided locally, typically within a **5 km radius** of the applicant’s residence. If work is provided beyond this distance, an additional **10% wage** is paid to the worker to meet extra transportation and living expenses.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**: Launched on **25 December 2000**, this is a nationwide plan in **India** to provide **all-weather road connectivity** to unconnected rural habitations. Unlike **MGNREGA**, it is an infrastructure project and not a wage employment guarantee scheme.

• **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)**: Launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** in **June 2011**, it aims to create efficient and effective institutional platforms for the rural poor, enabling them to increase household income through sustainable **livelihood enhancements** and improved access to **financial services**.

• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**: This is a restructured version of the **NRLM** that focuses on organizing the poor into **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and fostering **self-employment**. It emphasizes **skill development** and **entrepreneurship** rather than manual labor.

• **Social Audit**: A unique feature of **MGNREGA** is the mandatory **Social Audit**, which is conducted by the **Gram Sabha**. This process ensures **transparency** and **accountability** by allowing the community to monitor and verify the implementation of projects and expenditure.

• **Funding Mechanism**: The **Central Government** of **India** bears **100%** of the cost of wages for **unskilled manual labor** and **75%** of the material cost and wages for skilled or semi-skilled workers, while the remaining **25%** of material costs is borne by the **State Governments**.

**Important Points__**

• The scheme was originally launched as **NREGA** but was renamed the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** on **2 October 2009**, marking the birth anniversary of **Mahatma Gandhi**.

• The **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)** is the nodal agency at the **Central** level that oversees the policy framework and funding, while the **Gram Panchayats** are responsible for the actual implementation at the village level.

• Workers are issued a **Job Card**, which is a key document that records their rights and the amount of work they have completed. This card must be issued within **15 days** of application.

• Wages under **MGNREGA** are revised annually by the government and are linked to the **Consumer Price Index-Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** to ensure that the purchasing power of rural workers is maintained against **inflation**.

• The program has played a significant role in reducing **rural-to-urban migration** by providing viable employment opportunities within the villages during lean agricultural seasons.

questions.question: The phenomenon of interference in light waves is a direct consequence of:

options.text: The diffraction of light around obstacles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The superposition principle of waves.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The phenomenon of **interference** occurs when two or more light waves overlap in space, leading to a redistribution of light energy. This phenomenon is a direct consequence of the **superposition principle**.

• The **superposition principle** states that when two or more waves of the same type cross at the same point, the resultant displacement at that point is equal to the **vector sum** of the displacements of the individual waves.

• **Constructive Interference:** This occurs when the waves are in phase (crest meets crest or trough meets trough), leading to a wave with a larger amplitude and **maximum intensity**.

• **Destructive Interference:** This occurs when the waves are out of phase (crest meets trough), leading to a wave with a smaller amplitude or zero amplitude, resulting in **minimum intensity**.

• **Why other options are incorrect:**

• **Light as particles (photons):** This particle nature explains the **photoelectric effect** and **blackbody radiation**, but interference is a wave-like property.

• **Diffraction:** While diffraction involves the bending of light around obstacles and also utilizes superposition, interference specifically refers to the interaction between waves from **coherent sources**.

• **Polarization:** This refers to the orientation of the oscillations of a **transverse wave** in a particular direction and is not the cause of interference.

**Additional Information__**

• The most famous demonstration of light interference is **Young's Double-Slit Experiment**, conducted by **Thomas Young** in 1801, which provided definitive proof of the **wave nature of light**.

• To observe a stable interference pattern, the sources must be **coherent**, meaning they emit light waves of the same frequency and maintain a **constant phase difference** over time.

• In interference, energy is not lost but is simply **redistributed** from the regions of destructive interference (dark fringes) to the regions of constructive interference (bright fringes), obeying the **law of conservation of energy**.

• The condition for **constructive interference** is that the path difference must be an integral multiple of the wavelength: Delta x = nlambda (where n = 0, 1, 2...).

• The condition for **destructive interference** is that the path difference must be an odd multiple of half the wavelength: Delta x = (n + (1)/(2))lambda .
</ul

Consider the following statements about 'Bibi ka Maqbara':
1. It was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in memory of his wife.
2. It is located in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and is called the "Taj Mahal of the Deccan."
3. It was constructed in the early 1500s during Babur's reign.
Which among these following is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Bibi ka Maqbara** was commissioned by the **Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb** in **1660** in memory of his first wife and chief consort, **Dilras Banu Begum**. She was posthumously known as **Rabia-ud-Daurani**. While some historical records suggest that his son, **Azam Shah**, oversaw the construction, it was built during the reign of **Aurangzeb** to honor his wife. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The mausoleum is located in **Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar** (formerly known as **Aurangabad**) in the state of **Maharashtra**, **India**. It is famously called the **Taj of the Deccan** or **Dakkhani Taj** because its design was heavily inspired by the **Taj Mahal** in **Agra**. It stands as a major landmark and a symbol of **Mughal architecture** in the southern part of the empire. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• The construction of the **Bibi ka Maqbara** took place between **1651** and **1661 AD**, which is in the **17th century**. **Babur**, the founder of the **Mughal Empire**, reigned from **1526** to **1530 AD** in the **early 16th century**. Therefore, the monument was built more than a century after **Babur** reign ended. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• ***Hence, the correct answer is 1 and 2 only.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Architectural Details**: The monument was designed by the architect **Ata-ullah**, who was the son of **Ustad Ahmad Lahauri**, the principal designer of the **Taj Mahal**. This lineage explains the striking similarities between the two structures. The engineering work was carried out by **Hanspat Rai**.

• **Materials and Construction**: Unlike the **Taj Mahal**, which is constructed entirely of white **marble**, the **Bibi ka Maqbara** uses **marble** only for the main dome and the lattice screens. The rest of the structure is built with **basaltic trap** stone and finished with a fine **polished plaster** that gives it a marble-like appearance.

• **Garden Layout**: The tomb is set in the center of a **Charbagh** (four-fold garden) layout. It features axial ponds, fountains, and water channels, surrounded by high enclosure walls with **pavilions** and **minarets**.

• **Historical Context**: **Dilras Banu Begum** was a princess of the **Safavid dynasty** of **Persia**. She died in **1657** due to complications following the birth of her fifth child, **Akbar II**. Her death deeply affected **Aurangzeb**, leading to the commissioning of this grand tomb.

• **City Name Change**: The city where the monument is located, **Aurangabad**, was officially renamed **Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar** by the **Government of Maharashtra** in **2023**, in honor of the second **Chhatrapati** of the **Maratha Empire**.

**Important Points__**

• **Cost of Construction**: Historical inscriptions indicate that the mausoleum was built at a cost of approximately **6,68,203 Rupees** and **7 Annas**. This was significantly less than the cost of the **Taj Mahal**, which is why it is sometimes referred to as a more modest version of the **Agra** monument.

• **Comparison with Taj Mahal**: While the **Taj Mahal** represents the peak of **Mughal architecture** under **Shah Jahan**, the **Bibi ka Maqbara** reflects the transition and the beginning of the decline in the lavishness of **Mughal** buildings during **Aurangzeb** reign.

• **Tourism**: It is currently a protected monument under the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** and remains one of the most visited historical sites in **Maharashtra**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mughal mansabdari system is/are correct?**Statement I.** A mansab indicated both the rank (zat) and salary of a noble.**Statement II.** Every mansabdar was required to reside personally in the jagir whose revenue he drew.

options.text: Both I and II are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Mansabdari system** was the administrative and military framework of the **Mughal Empire**, introduced by Emperor **Akbar** in **1571**. It was designed to organize the nobility and ensure a steady supply of military troops for the state.

• **Statement I**: The term **Mansab** refers to a rank or position held by an official. Each **Mansabdar** was assigned a dual rank: **Zat** and **Sawar**. The **Zat** rank was a numerical value that indicated the personal status of the noble in the imperial hierarchy and directly determined the **salary** they were entitled to receive. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***

• **Statement II**: While **Mansabdars** were often remunerated through **Jagirs** (assignments of land revenue), they were not required to reside personally in the **Jagir** from which they drew their income. In fact, **Mughal** policy encouraged the frequent transfer of **Mansabdars** from one post to another to prevent them from developing local power bases or becoming independent rulers. They usually collected revenue from their assigned **Jagirs** through their agents, known as **Amils**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

• The system ensured that the **Emperor** maintained absolute control over the military and administrative officials by making their positions dependent on imperial favor rather than hereditary right.

• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only I.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Zat and Sawar Ranks**: The **Zat** rank fixed the personal status and **salary** of the officer, while the **Sawar** rank indicated the number of **cavalrymen** (horses and riders) the **Mansabdar** was required to maintain for the **Mughal** army.

• **Classification of Ranks**: There were approximately **33** to **66** grades of **Mansabdars**. The lowest rank was **10**, and the highest for commoners was generally **5,000**. Ranks above **5,000**, such as **7,000** or **10,000**, were typically reserved for **Princes** of the royal blood.

• **Payment Methods**: **Mansabdars** were classified into two types based on their payment: **Naqdi** (those paid in cash from the royal treasury) and **Jagirdars** (those paid through the assignment of land revenue from a specific territory).

• **Evolution under Later Emperors**:

• Emperor **Jahangir** introduced the **Du-aspa Sih-aspa** (two-horse, three-horse) system, which allowed him to increase the military strength of a **Mansabdar** without increasing his **Zat** rank or personal **salary**.

• Emperor **Shah Jahan** introduced the **Month-scale** or **Month-ratio** system to manage the discrepancy between the estimated revenue (**Jama**) and the actual revenue collected (**Hasil**) from the **Jagirs**.

**Important Points__**

• **Non-Hereditary Nature**: A **Mansab** was not hereditary. It was granted by the **Emperor** and could be revoked or changed at any time. Upon the death of a **Mansabdar**, his **Mansab** lapsed, and his property was often seized by the state under the **Law of Escheat** to settle any outstanding debts to the treasury.

• **Military Obligations**: Every **Mansabdar** had to bring his contingent for periodic inspection. To prevent fraud, **Akbar** enforced the **Dagh** (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive rolls of soldiers) systems, which were originally introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**.

• **Administrative Roles**: **Mansabdars** were not just military commanders; they also served as **Governors**, **Ministers**, and other high-ranking civil officials within the **Mughal** administration.
</ul

questions.question: What was the immediate outcome of Pakistan's objection to the SAARC Motor Vehicle Agreement in 2014?

questions.solution:

__

• The **BBIN MVA** was signed on **June 15, 2015**, in **Thimphu, Bhutan**, by the transport ministers of **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, and Nepal**.

• The proposal for a trilateral pact with **China** and **Bhutan** was never the outcome, as **China** is not a member of **SAARC** and **India** maintains a distinct strategic policy regarding connectivity with **China**. **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**

• While **India** has increased its engagement with **BIMSTEC**, the immediate outcome of the **2014** deadlock was specifically the **BBIN** road connectivity pact, not a maritime agreement. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**

__

• The **BBIN** initiative (**Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal**) is a sub-regional architecture aimed at improving economic integration through connectivity in power, water, and transport sectors.

• The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** has been the lead technical and financial advisor for the **BBIN** project under its **South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation (SASEC)** program.

• The **BBIN MVA** allows for **passenger, personal, and cargo vehicles** to travel across the borders of the four participating nations, reducing the cost and time of doing business.

**Important Points__**

• **SAARC** (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established on **December 8, 1985**, in **Dhaka**, with the goal of promoting the welfare of the people of **South Asia**.

• The **8 member states** of **SAARC** are **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka**.

• The failure of the **SAARC MVA** in **2014** highlighted the **consensus-based decision-making** flaw of the organization, where a single member can veto regional progress.

• This event accelerated **India’s** **'Neighborhood First'** policy and its **'Act East'** policy, prioritizing groups like **BIMSTEC** (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) over **SAARC**.

• The **BBIN** model is often cited as a successful example of **'minilateralism'** in **South Asia**, where smaller groups of countries collaborate on specific functional areas to achieve faster results.

questions.question: Read the following statements and choose the correct option:**Statement 1:** The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass situated to the south of the river Narmada.**Statement 2:** The Aravalli hills form the northern boundary of the Deccan Plateau.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• Statement 1: The **Deccan Plateau** is a **triangular landmass** that lies to the **south** of the **river Narmada**. It is one of the most significant physiographic units of **India** and forms a major part of the **Peninsular Plateau**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• Statement 2: The **Aravalli hills** are located on the **western** and **northwestern** margins of the **Peninsular Plateau**, specifically bordering the **Central Highlands**. The **northern** boundary of the **Deccan Plateau** is actually formed by the **Satpura range**, while the **Mahadev hills**, the **Kaimur hills**, and the **Maikal range** form its **eastern extensions**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Deccan Plateau** is higher in the **west** and slopes gently **eastwards**. This **geographical feature** is the reason why major **rivers** like the **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri** flow towards the **east** and drain into the **Bay of Bengal**.

• An extension of the **Deccan Plateau** is also visible in the **northeast**, locally known as the **Meghalaya**, **Karbi-Anglong Plateau**, and **North Cachar Hills**, separated by a fault from the **Chotanagpur Plateau**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Deccan Trap** is a distinct feature of the plateau, characterized by **black soil** of **volcanic origin**. These **igneous rocks** have denuded over time to create the fertile **regur soil**, which is ideal for **cotton cultivation**.

• The **Western Ghats** (also known as **Sahyadri**) and the **Eastern Ghats** mark the western and eastern boundaries of the **Deccan Plateau** respectively. The **Western Ghats** are continuous and higher, with an average elevation of **900 to 1600 metres**.

• The **Eastern Ghats** are lower, with an average elevation of **600 metres**, and are discontinuous because they are dissected by **rivers** flowing into the **Bay of Bengal**. They stretch from the **Mahanadi Valley** to the **Nilgiris** in the **south**.

• The **Western Ghats** cause **orographic rain** as they intercept the **southwest monsoon** winds. The height of the **Western Ghats** increases progressively from **north** to **south**.

• The **Deccan Plateau** covers an area of approximately **5 lakh square kilometres** and spans across several **Indian states**, including **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, **Telangana**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**.

**Important Points__**

• **Anai Mudi** is the highest peak of the **Peninsular Plateau** and the **Western Ghats**, standing at an elevation of **2,695 metres** in the state of **Kerala**.

• **Doda Betta** is another prominent peak in the **Western Ghats** with a height of **2,637 metres**. In contrast, **Mahendragiri** is the highest peak in the **Eastern Ghats**, located in **Odisha** at **1,501 metres**.

• The **Aravalli hills** are among the **oldest fold mountains** in the world, dating back to the **Pre-Cambrian era**. They are highly **denuded** and exist as **broken hills** extending from **Gujarat** to **Delhi**.

• The **Peninsular Plateau** is one of the **oldest landmasses** on earth, formed due to the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**. It consists of **broad and shallow valleys** and **rounded hills**.

• The **Central Highlands**, the other major division of the **Peninsular Plateau**, lies to the **north** of the **Narmada river** and covers a major part of the **Malwa Plateau**.
</ul

Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:**
Statement 1:** Adolescents constitute nearly one-fifth of India's total population.**
Statement 2:** Adolescents are grouped in the age bracket of 10 to 19 years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1** suggests that **adolescents** make up nearly **one-fifth** of the **total population** of **India**. According to the **Census of India 2011**, the **adolescent population** (individuals aged **10-19 years**) was recorded at approximately **253 million**, which accounts for about **20.9%** of the **country's** total **population**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2** defines the **age bracket** for **adolescents** as **10 to 19 years**. This specific **age group** is the standard definition provided by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** and is strictly followed by the **Government of India** for **demographic** analysis and **policy formulation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Adolescents** are considered the most significant **human resource** for the **future** of the **nation**. They are in a **transitional phase** from **childhood** to **adulthood**, which is marked by rapid **physical**, **mental**, and **emotional** changes.
 
• The **nutritional requirements** of **adolescents** are significantly higher than those of a **child** or an **adult**. Poor **nutrition** during this **period** can lead to **deficiency diseases** and stunted **growth**, which is why **government programs** focus heavily on this **demographic**.
 
• In **India**, the **adolescent population** is characterized by a large **number** of individuals who require **special attention** regarding **education**, **health**, and **vocational training** to harness the **demographic dividend**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Youth Policy (NYP-2014)**: While **adolescents** are aged **10-19 years**, the **National Youth Policy 2014** defines **youth** as persons in the **age group** of **15 to 29 years**. This helps in **categorizing** different **stages** of **development** for **targeted interventions**.
 
• **Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK)**: This **health program** was launched in **January 2014** by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**. It aims to reach out to **253 million** **adolescents** in **India**, focusing on **nutrition**, **reproductive health**, **substance abuse**, and **mental health**.
 
• **Anemia among Adolescents**: A critical **health issue** in **India** is the high **prevalence** of **Anemia**, particularly among **adolescent girls**. The **Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS)** program is a **government initiative** designed to address this **nutritional deficiency**.
 
• **Demographic Dividend**: **India** currently possesses a **youthful demographic profile**. The **adolescent** and **youth population** provides a **window of opportunity** for **economic growth**, provided there is adequate **investment** in their **skill development** and **health**.
 
• **Education and Literacy**: The **literacy rate** among **adolescents** has seen a **steady increase** over the **decades**, but **challenges** like **school dropouts** at the **secondary level** remain a **concern** for **policymakers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gender Concerns**: **Adolescent girls** often face **social barriers** such as **early marriage** and **restricted mobility**, which can impact their **educational** and **health outcomes** compared to **adolescent boys**.
 
• **Urban vs Rural Distribution**: A significant **portion** of **India's adolescents** resides in **rural areas**, where **access** to **quality healthcare** and **modern education** facilities is often **limited** compared to **urban centers**.
 
• **Right to Education (RTE)**: The **Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002** inserted **Article 21-A** to provide **free and compulsory education** to all **children** in the **age group** of **six to fourteen years**, which covers the **early adolescent** years.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**: **Empowering adolescents** is crucial for achieving **SDG 3** (Good Health and Well-being), **SDG 4** (Quality Education), and **SDG 5** (Gender Equality) by the **year 2030**.

questions.question: What is the role of FII in India economic reforms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Invest in India financial markets**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)** are entities such as **pension funds**, **mutual funds**, and **investment trusts** that are incorporated outside **India** and invest in the **Indian financial markets**.

• The primary role of **FII** in the context of **India's economic reforms** is to provide **liquidity** and **capital** to the **domestic stock exchanges** and **debt markets**. **Hence, statement 3 is correct.**

• **FIIs** do not provide **agriculture subsidies**, as subsidies are **fiscal tools** used by the **Government of India** to support **farmers** and are funded through the **Union Budget**. **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**

• **FIIs** do not invest in **government salaries**; these expenditures are **revenue expenditures** of the state, managed through **taxation** and **internal revenue**. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

• While **foreign capital** can flow into **infrastructure**, it is typically done through **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** or **External Commercial Borrowings (ECB)** rather than **FII**, which focuses on **secondary market** securities. **Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.**

• The entry of **FIIs** into **India** was a significant part of the **1991 Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms, aimed at **globalizing** the **Indian economy** and attracting **foreign exchange**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Regulation:** **FIIs** are strictly regulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** and must comply with the guidelines set by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** under the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)**.

• **Evolution to FPI:** In **2014**, **SEBI** introduced the **Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI)** regime, which merged **FIIs**, **Sub-accounts**, and **Qualified Foreign Investors (QFIs)** into a single category to simplify the **investment process**.

• **Market Impact:** **FII** inflows are often called **'hot money'** because they are highly **volatile** and can be withdrawn quickly based on **global economic conditions**, affecting the **value of the Indian Rupee** and **stock market indices** like **NIFTY** and **SENSEX**.

• **Investment Instruments:** **FIIs** invest in a variety of instruments including **equity shares**, **corporate bonds**, **government securities (G-Secs)**, and **units of mutual funds**.

• **Economic Significance:** Large **FII** inflows help **India** manage its **Current Account Deficit (CAD)** by providing the necessary **foreign currency** to balance **international payments**.

**Important Points__**

• **Participatory Notes (P-Notes):** These are **offshore derivative instruments** issued by **registered FIIs** to **overseas investors** who wish to invest in the **Indian stock markets** without registering themselves with **SEBI**.

• **Investment Limits:** The **Government of India** and **RBI** set specific **sectoral caps** and **aggregate investment limits** for **FIIs** to ensure that **foreign ownership** does not destabilize **strategic sectors**.

• **Comparison with FDI:** Unlike **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, which involves a **long-term physical investment** in **plant and machinery** or **management control**, **FII** is a **short-term to medium-term portfolio investment**.

• **Historical Context:** **India** opened its **capital markets** to **FIIs** in **September 1992**, which marked a turning point in the **depth** and **sophistication** of **Indian financial markets**.
</ul

questions.question:
Match the geological era/period with a characteristic life event:
1. Precambrian
2. Mesozoic
3. Cenozoic
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1-Origin of life, 2-Dinosaurs' dominance, 3-First mammals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Precambrian** period is the earliest and longest span of geological time, beginning with the formation of Earth approximately **4.6 billion years ago**. This era is characterized by the **Origin of life**, where the first **single-celled organisms**, such as **cyanobacteria** and **prokaryotic cells**, appeared in the oceans roughly **3.5 to 4 billion years ago**.
 
• The **Mesozoic Era**, spanning from about **252 to 66 million years ago**, is famously known as the **"Age of Reptiles."** Its primary characteristic was the **Dinosaurs' dominance** across terrestrial ecosystems during the **Triassic**, **Jurassic**, and **Cretaceous** periods.
 
• The **Cenozoic Era** began approximately **66 million years ago** and continues to the **present day**. It is commonly referred to as the **"Age of Mammals"** because, following the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs, **mammals** underwent rapid **evolution** and **diversification**, eventually becoming the dominant land animals.
 
• The classification of these events helps geologists and biologists understand the **evolutionary timeline** of Earth, matching the **Precambrian** with the **Origin of life**, the **Mesozoic** with **Dinosaurs**, and the **Cenozoic** with the rise and prominence of **Mammals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Precambrian Supereon**:
 
 
• It accounts for nearly **88%** of Earth's total geological history.
 
• It is divided into the **Hadean**, **Archean**, and **Proterozoic** eons.
 
• The **Oxygen Revolution** occurred during this time, where **photosynthetic organisms** began releasing oxygen into the **atmosphere**.
 
 
 
• **The Mesozoic Era Details**:
 
 
• This era saw the breakup of the supercontinent **Pangea** into the modern continents.
 
• In addition to dinosaurs, the first **birds** and **flowering plants (angiosperms)** appeared during this time.
 
• It ended with the **Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) mass extinction** event, likely caused by an **asteroid impact** in the **Yucatan Peninsula**.
 
 
 
• **The Cenozoic Era Structure**:
 
 
• It is divided into three periods: the **Paleogene**, **Neogene**, and **Quaternary**.
 
• The **Quaternary Period** (the last **2.6 million years**) is significant for the evolution and expansion of **Homo sapiens**.
 
• Significant **climatic changes**, including multiple **ice ages**, have shaped the current distribution of flora and fauna.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geological Time Scale (GTS)**: Scientists use the **GTS** to describe the timing and relationships of events that have occurred during Earth's history. It is measured in **Eons**, **Eras**, **Periods**, and **Epochs**.
 
• **Biological Transitions**: While **mammals** actually first appeared in the **Mesozoic** (Triassic period), they remained small and nocturnal; the **Cenozoic** marks their shift into the **"First mammals"** to achieve massive ecological dominance.

questions.question: Simplify: sqrt{75} + sqrt{48} - sqrt{27}

__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the common surd factor, which is √3.

√75 = 5√3

√27 = 3√3

**∴ The correct answer is 6√3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √75 + √48 − √27

**Formula:** √(a² × b) = a√b

⇒ √(25 × 3) + √(16 × 3) − √(9 × 3)

⇒ 5√3 + 4√3 − 3√3

⇒ (5 + 4 − 3) × √3

⇒ 9√3 − 3√3

⇒ 6√3

**∴ The correct answer is 6√3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Like Surds

Surds that have the same irrational part are called like surds and can be combined using basic arithmetic.

Simplest Form of a Surd

A surd is in its simplest form when the number under the radical has no perfect square factors other than 1.

Rationalization

questions.question: Find the least number which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5, 7, and 8.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The least number that leaves a remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z is LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Divisors: 5, 7, 8 (These are co-prime numbers).

LCM = 5 × 7 × 8 = 280.

Required Number = 280 + 3 = 283.

**∴ The correct answer is 283.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 5, 7, 8

Remainder = 3

**Formula Used:**

Least Number = [LCM of (Divisors)] + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d0f95bef11eeae65a4331dcc55df93d3334f54a14c3eb6bf0b218157044e90b.png] 

⇒ To find the LCM of 5, 7, and 8:

⇒ 5 = 5¹

⇒ 7 = 7¹

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 8 × 5 × 7 = 280

⇒ Required Number = 280 + 3

⇒ Required Number = 283

**∴ The correct answer is 283.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

When numbers have no common factors other than 1, their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is simply the product of the numbers.

General Remainder Case

If the remainders are different (r₁, r₂, r₃) such that (divisor − remainder) = k (a constant), then the number is LCM(divisors) − k.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rationalize the middle term: 1 / (3 − √8) = 3 + √8.

The expression becomes: (3 + √8) + (3 + √8) − (6 + 4√2).

Combine like terms: 6 + 2√8 − (6 + 4√2).

Result: 6 + 4√2 − 6 − 4√2 = 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3 + √8) + (1 / (3 − √8)) − (6 + 4√2)

**Formula Used:** Rationalization of denominator: 1 / (a − b) = (a + b) / (a² − b²)

⇒ First, simplify √8 = √(4 × 2) = 2√2.

⇒ Rationalize the term 1 / (3 − √8):

⇒ 1 / (3 − √8) × (3 + √8) / (3 + √8) = (3 + √8) / (3² − (√8)²)

⇒ (3 + √8) / (9 − 8) = 3 + √8 = 3 + 2√2.

⇒ Substitute the rationalized value back into the expression:

⇒ (3 + 2√2) + (3 + 2√2) − (6 + 4√2)

⇒ (3 + 3) + (2√2 + 2√2) − 6 − 4√2

⇒ 6 + 4√2 − 6 − 4√2

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator of the form (a − √b), multiply both the numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + √b).

Conjugate Pairs

The product of conjugate surds (a + √b) and (a − √b) is always a rational number: a² − b.

Simplifying Radicals

A radical √x can be simplified by factoring out the largest perfect square: √8 = √(4 × 2) = 2√2.</p

questions.question: P and Q invest ₹1,00,000 and ₹50,000, respectively. After one year, the total profit, which includes a 10% interest, amounts to ₹20,000. Determine Q's share of the profit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹6,666.67**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Investment ratio **P : Q** = 1,00,000 : 50,000 = **2 : 1**.

Interest on capital (10%) = ₹10,000 for **P** and ₹5,000 for **Q**.

Total interest = ₹15,000. Remaining profit = ₹20,000 − ₹15,000 = ₹5,000.

**Q**'s total share = Interest + (1/3 × Remaining Profit).

**Q**'s share = 5,000 + (5,000 ÷ 3) = 5,000 + 1,666.67 = ₹6,666.67.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,666.67.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of **P** = ₹1,00,000

Investment of **Q** = ₹50,000

Total Profit (including interest) = ₹20,000

Interest Rate = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Profit Share = Interest on Capital + (Investment Ratio × Surplus Profit)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f9ac6bb99bca84ef38d2f8b682e88302b06362c92b25f0d59b157db8c2f5f18.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest on **P**'s capital = 10% of 1,00,000 = ₹10,000

⇒ Interest on **Q**'s capital = 10% of 50,000 = ₹5,000

⇒ Total Interest = 10,000 + 5,000 = ₹15,000

⇒ Remaining Profit = Total Profit − Total Interest = 20,000 − 15,000 = ₹5,000

⇒ Investment Ratio **P : Q** = 1,00,000 : 50,000 = 2 : 1

⇒ **Q**'s share of remaining profit = (1 ÷ (2 + 1)) × 5,000 = 1/3 × 5,000 = ₹1,666.67

⇒ Total share of **Q** = Interest + Profit share = 5,000 + 1,666.67 = ₹6,666.67

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,666.67.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit Sharing Ratio

In a partnership, profit is shared in the ratio of (Capital × Time). If time is constant, it is shared in the ratio of Capital.

Interest on Capital

Interest on capital is a prior charge on profits. It is calculated on the individual capital of each partner before the remaining profit is distributed.

Working vs. Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive a salary/commission, while a sleeping partner only invests capital.

questions.question: The mean of five consecutive odd numbers is 61. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any set of **consecutive odd numbers**, the **mean** is always the **middle term**.

Since there are 5 numbers, the 3rd number is the mean.

Middle term (3rd) = 61

Smallest term (1st) = 61 − (2 × 2) = 57

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mean of 5 consecutive odd numbers = 61

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b512878a6b4a2b50b60c301aefd6f01ed994d2c3e6418cd47804337aa094c142.png] 

Let the five consecutive odd numbers be x, x+2, x+4, x+6, and x+8.

⇒ (x + x+2 + x+4 + x+6 + x+8) ÷ 5 = 61

⇒ 5x + 20 = 61 × 5

⇒ 5x + 20 = 305

⇒ 5x = 305 − 20

⇒ 5x = 285

⇒ x = 285 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 57

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean of Arithmetic Progression

For any series in A.P., Mean = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd natural numbers is always n².

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n consecutive odd natural numbers is simply n.</p

questions.question: The sum of 25% of a number and 40% of the same number is 325. What is 120% of that number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Combined percentage = 25% + 40% = 65%

Given: 65% of the number = 325

1% of the number = 325 ÷ 65 = 5

Required value = 120% of the number = 5 × 120 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of 25% and 40% of a **number** is 325.

**Formula Used:**

Value = (Percentage / 100) × Total Number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96ca4ff7d9d53b8d2e7ec0ebddae0f84c6e2a38703c8402e0c1e7973d0f2fb4e.png] 

Let the number be **x**.

⇒ (25/100) × x + (40/100) × x = 325

⇒ (25 + 40)/100 × x = 325

⇒ 65/100 × x = 325

⇒ x = (325 × 100) / 65

⇒ x = 5 × 100 = 500

Now, calculate 120% of 500:

⇒ Required value = (120/100) × 500

⇒ Required value = 1.2 × 500

⇒ Required value = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Addition Rule

When percentages are calculated on the **same base** (the same number), they can be added or subtracted directly. Example: a% of x + b% of x = (a + b)% of x.

Fraction Equivalents

Knowing common fractions helps speed up calculations: 25% = 1/4, 40% = 2/5, and 120% = 6/5.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Old Value) / Old Value] × 100. This is useful for profit, loss, and growth questions.</p

**__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate Formula

For two successive interest periods with rate r%, the effective rate is given by (r + r + r²/100)%.

Compounding Frequency Rule

When interest is compounded every 'k' months, the rate becomes R × (k/12) and the number of periods becomes (Total months / k).

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 periods is P × (r/100)².

questions.question: A 90-litre mixture of petrol and kerosene is in the ratio 4:5. Some of it is removed and replaced with pure petrol. The final ratio becomes 7:5. How much of the mixture was replaced?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio (Petrol : Kerosene) = 4 : 5 (Total 9 units)

Final Ratio (Petrol : Kerosene) = 7 : 5 (Total 12 units)

Since only petrol is added, Kerosene quantity in final 90 L = (5 ÷ 12) × 90 = 37.5 L.

Initial Kerosene quantity = (5 ÷ 9) × 90 = 50 L.

Fraction of mixture remaining = Final Kerosene ÷ Initial Kerosene = 37.5 ÷ 50 = 3/4.

Quantity replaced = (1 − 3/4) × 90 = 22.5 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5 litres.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial volume = 90 L, Initial ratio = 4:5, Final ratio = 7:5.

**Formula Used:** Quantity of component not added remains constant in the remaining mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/887ace774558c3931d4dc4bc791511c822f696d0c37c6d340a5b059b25bd67de.png] 

⇒ Initial Petrol = (4/9) × 90 = 40 L

⇒ Initial Kerosene = (5/9) × 90 = 50 L

⇒ Let x L of mixture be replaced by x L of petrol.

⇒ Kerosene remaining after removal = 50 − (5/9)x

⇒ Final Kerosene in 90 L mixture = (5/12) × 90 = 37.5 L

⇒ 50 − (5/9)x = 37.5

⇒ (5/9)x = 50 − 37.5 = 12.5

⇒ x = (12.5 × 9) ÷ 5 = 2.5 × 9 = 22.5 L

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5 litres.**

**__Additional Information__**

Replacement Formula

Alligation Rule

questions.question: A train crosses a 180-meter-long platform in 20 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The train covers its own length in 12 seconds and (Length + 180 m) in 20 seconds.

The extra distance of 180 m is covered in the extra time: 20 − 12 = 8 seconds.

Speed of the train = 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5 m/s.

Length of the train = Speed × Time to cross the man = 22.5 × 12 = 270 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 270 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of platform = 180 m

Time taken to cross platform = 20 s

Time taken to cross man = 12 s

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/951b4b33c17d2cf6a3351cdb925d1e8c09f67f85ef57fc48127b945e3c1d3339.png] 

⇒ Let the length of the train be L meters.

⇒ Speed of the train while crossing the man = L ÷ 12

⇒ Speed of the train while crossing the platform = (L + 180) ÷ 20

⇒ Equating the speeds: L ÷ 12 = (L + 180) ÷ 20

⇒ 20 × L = 12 × (L + 180)

⇒ 20L = 12L + 2160

⇒ 20L − 12L = 2160

⇒ 8L = 2160

⇒ L = 2160 ÷ 8

⇒ L = 270 m

**∴ The correct answer is 270 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Crossing a Stationary Point

When a train crosses a point object like a pole or a man, the distance covered is exactly the length of the train.

Crossing a Stationary Object with Length

When a train crosses a platform or a bridge, the total distance covered is the sum of the train length and the object length.

Relative Speed

Relative speed in the same direction is S₁ − S₂, and in the opposite direction, it is S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: An item is produced by one of three machines, A, B, or C. Machine A produces 50% of the items, B produces 30%, and C produces 20%. The defect rates are 1% for A, 2% for B, and 3% for C. If an item is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is defective?

Total Defect % = (ShareA × RateA) + (ShareB × RateB) + (ShareC × RateC)

Total Defect % = (50% × 1%) + (30% × 2%) + (20% × 3%)

Total Defect % = 0.5% + 0.6% + 0.6% = 1.7%

Probability = 1.7 / 100 = 0.017

**∴ The correct answer is 0.017.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Production shares: P(A) = 0.50, P(B) = 0.30, P(C) = 0.20

Defect rates: P(D|A) = 0.01, P(D|B) = 0.02, P(D|C) = 0.03

**Formula:**

Total Probability P(D) = P(A)×P(D|A) + P(B)×P(D|B) + P(C)×P(D|C)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/472722c0e3cdf7eb8a4728bc8dadc314ce264b5ab6f78c499447dc8f7b6348a4.png] 

⇒ P(D) = (0.50 × 0.01) + (0.30 × 0.02) + (0.20 × 0.03)

⇒ P(D) = 0.005 + 0.006 + 0.006

⇒ P(D) = 0.017

**∴ The correct answer is 0.017.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Probability Theorem

It calculates the probability of an event based on several mutually exclusive and exhaustive scenarios: P(E) = Σ P(Sᵢ) × P(E|Sᵢ).

Bayes' Theorem

Used to find the probability of a cause given an effect: P(A|D) = [P(A) × P(D|A)] ÷ P(D).

Complementary Events

The probability of an item being non-defective is calculated as P(Not D) = 1 − P(D).</p

questions.question: Complement of angle x is equal to (x + 10). Find the angle.

Sum of complementary angles = 90°.

Difference between the angle and its complement = 10°.

Smaller angle (x) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2

Angle = x

⇒ 2x + 10 = 90°

⇒ 2x = 80°

Two angles are called supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines, whose sum is always 180°.

Reflex Angle

An angle which is greater than 180° but less than 360°.</p

Using the identity sec²A − tan²A = 1 ⇒ (secA + tanA)(secA − tanA) = 1.

Adding both equations: (secA + tanA) + (secA − tanA) = x + 1/x.

⇒ (secA + tanA) + (secA − tanA) = x + 1/x

⇒ 2secA = (x² + 1) / x

questions.question: What is the x-intercept of the line 4x - 5y = 20 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the x-intercept, simply set y = 0 in the given equation.

4x − 5(0) = 20

4x = 20 ⇒ x = 5

The coordinate of the x-intercept is (5, 0).

**∴ The correct answer is (5, 0).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation of the line: 4x − 5y = 20

**Formula Used:**

Intercept form of a line: x/a + y/b = 1, where 'a' is the x-intercept and 'b' is the y-intercept.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3a6a8e55d8e03b6dea18d5c20fb56a822941c84ea817a8c4d72487c6f99a184.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4x − 5y = 20

⇒ Divide the entire equation by 20 to get 1 on the RHS:

⇒ (4x / 20) − (5y / 20) = 20 / 20

⇒ x / 5 − y / 4 = 1

⇒ x / 5 + y / (−4) = 1

⇒ Comparing with x/a + y/b = 1, we get a = 5.

⇒ The x-intercept is the point where the line crosses the x-axis, i.e., (a, 0).

⇒ x-intercept = (5, 0)

**∴ The correct answer is (5, 0).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Y-intercept

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation y = mx + c represents a line with slope 'm' and y-intercept 'c'. For 4x − 5y = 20, y = (4/5)x − 4.

Slope of a Line

questions.question: A quadrilateral ABCD has a circle inscribed within it. Given that the lengths of sides AB, BC, and CD are 6 cm, 7 cm, and 8 cm respectively, what is the length of side AD?

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

"So great was his shock that he could barely utter a word," said the nurse.

options.text: The nurse said he was shocked greatly and barely spoke.
The nurse said his shock was so great that he had barely spoken.
The nurse said that so great had his shock been that he could barely utter a word.
The nurse said that his shock was so great that he could barely utter a word.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The nurse said that his shock was so great that he could barely utter a word.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Normalizing the Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The direct speech uses an inverted, emphatic structure (**"So great was his shock..."**). In indirect speech, exclamatory or inverted sentences typically revert to the standard declarative word order (Subject + Verb). Thus, it becomes **"his shock was so great..."**
 
 
 
• **Tense and Verbs:**
 
 
• While the simple past (**"was"**) can sometimes change to the past perfect ("had been"), in sentences describing a continuous state or an established fact alongside an action, keeping the simple past is often preferred for natural phrasing once the structure is normalized.
 
• The modal verb **"could"** expresses ability in the past and does not change its form in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Clause:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"said"** remains unchanged, and the conjunction **"that"** is added to connect it to the reported statement.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The nurse said that his shock was so great that he could barely utter a word.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The nurse said he was shocked greatly and barely spoke."

 
 
• Incorrect because it fundamentally alters the vocabulary, sentence structure, and original meaning of the quote rather than accurately reporting it.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "The nurse said his shock was so great that he had barely spoken."
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the meaning from an inability to speak (**"could barely utter"**) to the mere fact that he didn't speak (**"had barely spoken"**).
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The nurse said that so great had his shock been that he could barely utter a word."
 
 
• Incorrect because it retains the inverted word order (**"so great had his shock been"**). In indirect speech, retaining this inversion in a subordinate clause is grammatically awkward; it must be converted to standard Subject + Verb order.
